The key activities of the Improvement of Crop Statistics scheme are the sample check on area enumeration of selected survey/sub-division numbers of the Khasra Register (Adangal) maintained by the Village Administrative Officers and the supervision of Crop Cutting Experiments for some important food crops in State-wide selected sample villages under this scheme.

improvements in the quality of primary data in respect of both Crop Area and Yield Estimation in the State.

The Agriculture Census is a Central Sector Scheme undertaken in Tamil Nadu under the aegis of the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India. The Directorate of Economics and Statistics is the Nodal Directorate for the conduct of the Agriculture Census in Tamil Nadu.

1.Preparation and enforcement of land use planning and zoning regulations incorporating infrastructure and

hazard restrictions.

It is proposed that formal land use planning and zoning regulations shall mandatorily incorporate critical parameters such as the availability of trunk infrastructure, including water supply, electricity, and sanitation systems, to ensure that development is aligned with service capabilities. Further, hazard mapping shall form an integral component of planning, identifying areas where development is prohibited due to natural hazards. In addition, hazard maps_ shall specify minimum separation between residential zones and hazardous occupancies. Accordingly, it is proposed to mandate the preparation and enforcement of land use plans and zoning regulations incorporating mandatory infrastructure requirements

and hazard-based restrictions.

2.Hazard maps shall be formally approved and published with prohibited zones, separation distances, no

construction areas

Further, hazard maps identifying prohibited zones, minimum separation distances, and no-construction areas shall be prepared, duly approved by the competent authority, and published for public access to ensure transparency and

awareness and implementation.

3.Establishing a regulatory framework to define zoning parameters based on availability of trunk infrastructure

There is a need to establishing a regulatory framework that defines zoning parameters based on the availability and adequacy of trunk infrastructure. This framework shall ensure that development permissions are granted only where infrastructure systems are sufficient or planned to meet the projected demand, thereby preventing overburdening of services and ensuring orderly growth.

4. The above proposed measures are expected to result in a scientifically robust and legally enforceable planning system that promotes sustainable development, enhances public safety, protects natural resources, and ensures efficient utilization of infrastructure. It will also improve transparency, strengthen governance, and support informed decision-making.

5. In view of the above, the Commissioner of Town and Country Planning has requested the Government. issue necessary orders mandating the integration of infrastructure availability and hazard considerations into land use planning and zoning regulations, approving -and publishing hazard maps indicating prohibited zones, separation distances, and no-construction areas, and establishing a- regulatory framework to define zoning parameters based on the availability of trunk infrastructure.

6. After careful consideration, the Government hereby, accept the request of Commissioner of Town and Country Planning and issue orders for mandating the integration of infrastructure availability and hazard considerations into land use planning and zoning regulations, approving and publishing hazard maps indicating prohibited zones, separation distances, and. no-construction areas, and establishing a regulatory framework to define zoning parameters based on the availability of trunk infrastructure.

The family of a Government servant faces financial hardship when the Government servant dies while in service. To alleviate such hardship, an eligible legal heir of the deceased Government servant was provided an employment under the Scheme of Compassionate Grounds Appointment which was introduced by the Government in the year 1972.

In order to further streamline the scheme, the Labour Welfare and Skill Development Department issued the Tamil Nadu Civil

(iii)

(v)

Subsequently, the administration of the scheme was transferred from the Labour Welfare and Skill Development Department to Human Resources Management Department in 20253.

Under the scheme, each Department was treated as a separate unit. Compassionate ground appointments were provided by the respective Departments to the legal heirs of deceased Government servants based on the seniority within that Department.

The MVUs bring veterinary services to the

doorsteps of livestock farmers, particularly in

remote and underserved areas. Each unit visits

three villages a day according to a scheduled

programme, while farmers can also avail

themselves of doorstep veterinary care by calling

the toll-free number 1962.

The initiative focuses on improving animal

health and fertility through timely treatment,

preventive care and artificial insemination, while

also creating awareness among farmers on

improved livestock management practices.

TAHDCO has registered tribal associations under an integrated organization called the Tamil Nadu Adi Dravidar and Tribal Advancement Society (TATAS) in accordance with the Tamil Nadu Societies Registration Act, 1975 across Tamil Nadu, with the objective of improving the livelihoods and socio-economic status of tribal communities. WHEREAS, the Government of Tamil Nadu is deeply committed to the conservation of Asiatic Elephants and intends to notify elephant corridors, so as to ensure the unobstructed movement of Asian Elephants (Elephas maximus), long-term survival of the species and to mitigate human-wildlife conflict;

AND WHEREAS a Committee has been constituted by the Government vide G.O. (D) No. 296, Environment, Climate Change and Forests (FR.5) Department, dated 26.12.2022, to identify and delineate the corridors and the Committee has submitted its report to the Government through the Principal Chief Conservator of Forests and Chief Wildlife Warden of the State;

AND WHEREAS for the aforesaid purposes, the Government of Tamil Nadu after careful consideration of the said reports have decided to notify the areas mentioned in the Schedule below as Jawalagiri - Ulibanda - Thaggatti Elephant Corridor with effect from the date of publication of this notification.

THE SCHEDULE

I. Name of the Elephant Corridor: Jawalagiri - Ulibanda — Thaggatti II. Description of the Elephant Corridor:

This corridor starts and ends in Ulibanda Reserve Forest of Cauvery South Wildlife Sanctuary by connecting two large habitats i.e. Jawalagiri Reserve Forest in Cauvery North Wildlife Sanctuary and Thaggatty Reserve Forest in Cauvery South Wildlife Sanctuary. The length of the elephant corridor is 18.5 km and the width ranges from 0.73 km to 3.20 km over an extent 3241.53 hectare. It is regular elephant movement along the Madeshvara halla stream (Madeswaran koivai) which connects above two large habitats. Subsequently elephants enter the Thaggatty Reserve Forest and further to Anchetty Reserve Forest.

Devotimaduvu hall, Javugu halla, Rangana Halla, Ichimaduvu Halla, Madesvara halla are the major valley/streams in the Ulibanda Reserve Forest and it further runs up to River Cauvery. This corridor will enable the Trans-Cauvery migration of elephants and other large mammals between the states of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. There is no Bottleneck located in this corridor. The above Reserve Forests, namely Ulibanda and Thaggatty forms part of Cauvery South Wildlife Sanctuary which was notified during 2022 and Jawalagiri Reserve Forest is part of the Cauvery North Wildlife Sanctuary, which was declared in the year 2014.

5.3.2.3. Price Support Scheme

With the objective of protecting farmers from

price declines during the harvest season, the

“Price Support Scheme” is being implemented for

agricultural commodities such as pulses and

copra.

228

Under this scheme, when the market price of

commodities such as pulses (blackgram,

greengram, and redgram) and copra falls below

the Minimum Support Price (MSP), procurement is

undertaken at the MSP for produce meeting the

Fair Average Quality (FAQ) standards. The Tamil

Nadu State Agricultural Marketing Board

(TNSAMB) functions as the State-level agency,

while the National Agricultural Cooperative

Marketing Federation of India (NAFED) and the

National Cooperative Consumers’ Federation of

India (NCCF) function as the Central procurement

agencies. Regulated Markets serve as the Primary

Procurement Centres.

In 2026, 974.80 metric tonnes of greengram

worth Rs.8.55 crore were procured from

1,098 farmers.
